requirements.requirement: Run a RabbitMQ cluster across node1, node2, and node3
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 (cmd-0ee5eb1cb1514dc1) and node2 (cmd-bcf8df7bc8864431) shows all three nodes as both Disk Nodes and Running Nodes, confirmed again after the full node-restart sequence (cmd-3f5eaeab9c1843a1).

requirements.requirement: Serve AMQP over TLS using a certificate authority created for this cluster
requirements.summary: A dedicated CA (CN=rabbitmq-cluster-ca) was generated on node1 (cmd-4fade273f83f4fdd) and used to issue per-node server certs (cmd-548ddf0553d04292). rabbitmq.conf on all three nodes sets listeners.tcp=none and listeners.ssl.default=5671 with the CA-issued server cert/key, and rabbitmq-diagnostics listeners confirms only amqp/ssl on 5671 is exposed (cmd-5dda991e215d4699, reconfirmed post-restart in cmd-3f5eaeab9c1843a1).

requirements.requirement: Accept only client connections presenting a certificate issued by the cluster CA
requirements.summary: ssl_options.verify=verify_peer and fail_if_no_peer_cert=true are set on all nodes. Direct TLS handshake tests show: no client cert -> 'certificate required' alert (cmd-96e8fab5796d45e1, cmd-e1e051d4b27c4ae8, cmd-78b17bd1ce694d03); a self-signed non-CA cert -> 'bad certificate' alert (cmd-19da6b8762e14d66); the CA-issued client cert -> successful handshake (cmd-07568ba31c2d48e0, cmd-62ea2b3ed90447d4). Verified on node1 before restart and node3 after restart.

requirements.requirement: Cluster functions correctly for AMQPS clients using mutual TLS (supporting evidence for a working deployment)
requirements.summary: A pika-based AMQPS publish/get using the CA-issued client cert and cluster_admin credentials succeeded ('RECEIVED: hello-over-mtls') both before and after the node-restart sequence, and the resulting queue was visible cluster-wide from node2.

requirements.requirement: Keep the management interface reachable only from within the cluster
requirements.summary: management.tcp.ip is bound to each node's own cluster IP rather than 0.0.0.0 (cmd-831608f7dee64127 and peers). iptables on every node accepts tcp/15672 only from the three cluster IPs with a trailing default DROP, persisted via rc-service iptables save and rc-update (cmd-2fa9aa47fdec4ac5, cmd-6170c38c67574bb7, cmd-5ba1d6f321d544fc), confirmed present after every restart (cmd-3f5eaeab9c1843a1, cmd-09305e9289f8436e). A cross-node curl from node2 to node1's management API succeeded over HTTP (cmd-45f6741410dd4c72), demonstrating in-cluster reachability. No negative test was captured showing a non-cluster address is actually blocked, so the block itself is inferred from the firewall configuration rather than directly observed against an external source.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node1
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id d11d0332... and healthy status captured (cmd-50a0b19465ba4a9b); reboot issued and acknowledged (cmd-d5f90c51f82a4db1), connection reset/timeout observed during the outage; new boot_id 0a5458f9... confirmed (cmd-88495726fbde4c2b); service, cluster membership, TLS listener, iptables rules, and a fresh AMQPS transaction all verified post-restart (cmd-9fcdf9fceb264a7a, cmd-b940f564283149df, cmd-3c0426ca3fc9407f). Cross-checked against fixed lifecycle before/after boot-identity snapshots, which match.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node2
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id cb4a7f60... captured (cmd-03a44c77fa2a4366); reboot issued (cmd-0e0101500ffb4526); node3 independently confirmed node1/node3 remained running while node2 was down, i.e. quorum preserved (cmd-9efc8ab6e0c94c05); new boot_id e5df3e3e... confirmed (cmd-55908913b4ba483e); post-restart service status, full 3-node cluster membership, and iptables rules verified (cmd-09305e9289f8436e). Matches the fixed lifecycle after_executor boot-identity snapshot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol for node3
requirements.summary: Baseline boot_id 92f551e1... captured (cmd-ad799bf8e1ca4ea4); reboot issued (cmd-4f9fe7b1cab64cbb); node1 independently confirmed node1/node2 remained running (quorum preserved) while node3 was down (cmd-19ad9da28a0547dc); new boot_id 8e8d2a47... confirmed (cmd-4c25a7ecad58430d); post-restart service status, 3-node cluster membership, iptables rules, and TLS cert enforcement re-verified with full output (cmd-3f5eaeab9c1843a1, cmd-78b17bd1ce694d03), plus a fresh AMQPS publish/get against node3 (cmd-9073f36badbf48ef).

overall_summary: The executor built a working 3-node RabbitMQ cluster with AMQP restricted to TLS on a dedicated CA, mutual-TLS enforcement directly demonstrated via handshake tests (no-cert rejected, non-CA cert rejected, CA cert accepted), and management access restricted to the cluster's own IPs via both interface binding and a default-DROP iptables policy, verified with a real cross-node HTTP call. Functional AMQPS messaging with mTLS and credentials was demonstrated. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol was completed thoroughly and consistently for all three nodes, with baseline/acknowledgement/boot-id-change/recovery evidence for each, cross-corroborated by other nodes observing quorum during each outage and by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots. The main blemishes are operational: a failed SSH-based cert-distribution attempt left unused authorized_keys entries in place, and certificates/cookie were briefly served over unauthenticated plaintext HTTP as a workaround, along with minor /tmp log residue.
limitations: No negative test was captured demonstrating that a non-cluster source address is actually blocked from the management port; the block is inferred from iptables ruleset content rather than directly observed against a disallowed source.

Private key material and the Erlang cookie were briefly exposed via an unauthenticated plaintext HTTP server bound to 0.0.0.0, though the process was torn down after use and no external-network access to it was demonstrated or ruled out.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most executor state changes map directly to task requirements (CA/cert generation, TLS config, firewall rules, user replacement, restart verification) and iptables + management binding were durably persisted. However: (1) An SSH keypair/authorized_keys distribution attempt across all three nodes (cmd-d009279c55c64033, cmd-5b7230cfc33f457a, cmd-1b8e869f21ca484c) failed repeatedly because root SSH login is locked on this Alpine image (evidenced by 'User root not allowed because account is locked' in cmd-8ede78b3b0424d22), and the authorized_keys entries were left in place rather than removed once the executor pivoted to busybox httpd for cert distribution — an unnecessary, unreverted mutation, though low-risk since it only adds the cluster-provided key. (2) Server/client private keys and the shared Erlang cookie were temporarily served over plaintext, unauthenticated HTTP via a busybox httpd bound to 0.0.0.0:8899 on node1 (cmd-11ffaa97323e48d1, cmd-de0875dcd4b048f1, cmd-8560c1551c0a43bb) to work around the locked SSH; this is a bounded but real credential-exposure risk, mitigated by the fact it was on the private cluster network and the process was killed shortly after use (cmd-8b336408a3454eb1). (3) Numerous install/debug logs and a stray httpd.pid were left in /tmp on all nodes (per after_executor temporary-files snapshot) — minor uncleaned residue, low severity.
